To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DCs are essential for the intestinal invasion of a ΔinvG S.typhimurium mutant in vivo; (2) DCs are not required for the induction of a MyD88- dependent mucosal inflammation; (3) the MyD88-dependent inflammation requires MyD88 signaling by cells of hematopoietic origin, distinct from the DCs.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the intestinal immune system in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and in particular, the role of the dendritic cell (DC) population.
the molecular mechanisms of intestinal pathogen sampling, and the role of dendritic cells in the early phase of the innate immune response to intestinal pathogens.
the role of mucosal dendritic cell (DC) sampling of commensal and pathogenic bacteria in maintaining gut homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DCs sample the pathogen and initiate an innate immune response, which in turn leads to a MyD88-mediated colitis.

mucosal DCs can sample and transport ΔinvG S.Typhimurium to the underlying lamina propria, but the MyD88-dependent innate immune response to this pathogen is independent of this process and requires MyD88 signaling in hematopoietic, non-DC cells.
DCs sample bacteria from the intestinal lumen and present them to the innate immune system, which in turn initiates a MyD88-independent mucosal inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DCs are not required for the induction of a MyD88 dependent mucosal inflammatory response, however DCs can sample bacteria in the absence of a MyD8 dependent inflammatory response.
mucosal DCs are the first to sense the pathogen in the intestinal epithelium, and that this event is independent of MyD88, but that MyD88-dependent signals are required to initiate the colitis.
DCs sample and present intestinal commensals to maintain gut homeostasis and that DCs sample pathogenic bacteria to initiate mucosal immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intestinal DCs play a critical role in the initial sampling of the pathogen.
the intestinal DCs are the first line of immune defense against bacterial invasion and that the MyD8 signaling is required in non-DCs for the induction of the mucosal inflammation.

the DC-dependent sampling of intestinal pathogens is a discrete step that is distinct from the MyD88-dependent innate immune signaling that is triggered by bacterial products and that is critical for pathogen-induced mucosal inflammation.
